name: Zach Lieberman
bio: Zach Lieberman (born 1977) is an artist, researcher and educator who uses code to make poetic, playful, often interactive work. He co-created openFrameworks, an open-source C++ toolkit for creative coding, with Theo Watson and Arturo Castro. In 2009 he worked with the Graffiti Research Lab, Free Art and Technology and others on the EyeWriter, a low-cost eye-tracking system that let the graffiti artist TEMPT1, paralysed by ALS, draw again with his eyes. In 2013 he co-founded the School for Poetic Computation in New York, an artist-run school about art, code and hardware. He has posted a new generative sketch almost every day since 2016, and leads the Future Sketches group at the MIT Media Lab, which looks at the history of computational art and drawing.
studyNotes: Sketch every day. A daily practice of small experiments in code builds a personal visual language and a huge archive of ideas.
Build tools and share them. openFrameworks and the EyeWriter are open-source; making tools others can use is part of the art.
Code with care. The EyeWriter shows technology made with and for a specific person, with a clear human purpose.
Teaching as practice. The School for Poetic Computation treats education itself as a creative work.
